page.layout: One printed page. One text column with a left-margin reference beside its first line and a Greek marginal note beside "Sic argumentatur". Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: Gen.4.14. Et illud de eodem: Egressus est Cain à facie Iehouae: v.16. Ex hac concessione[?] liquet, qualem Deum homo consternatus sibi fingat, uidelicet, alienū prorsus à miseris, implacabilem, ignem consumentem. Heb.12.29.Deut.4.24. Ne-que uero raro fit, ut etiam electi, serenae faciei Dei conspectu ad tepus orbati, re-probis se haud dissimiles esse opinentur.

Ἀντιπαγωγὴ[?] autem eluctantis & emerge-tis ex istis fluctibus fidei, haec est: Fretus tamen immensa tua potentia & misericordia, spero me in templo tuo εὐχαριστικὰ[?] sacrificia tibi oblaturum esse, summo cum meo gaudio. Scio enim te uiam inuenire posse, & apud te non esse illum uerbū impossibile. Luc.1.37.
main_text.head: Παραλλήλον.[?]
main_text.p: Et ego dicebam dum festinare: Excisus sum ab oculis tuis: uerum audisti uocem deprecationum mearum, cum clamare ad te. Psal.31,23.[?]
main_text.head: THESIS.
main_text.p: Vt cum desperationis tentatione ue-hementer luctatur fides: sic eam tandem fortiter insurgens uincit.

page.notes: Gen.4.14. is set at the left edge beside the first line; it is treated as a marginal reference. The Greek word before "sacrificia" (read as εὐχαριστικὰ) is hard to make out and is marked [?]. The Greek heading "Παραλλήλον." and the Greek margin note "ἰσχύς." are also uncertain. "Psal.31,23." is printed in a worn form and is marked [?]. The first word of the first paragraph ("concessione") is not clear and is marked [?]. The printed "ꝝ" in the Psalm reference is read as a comma. No Hebrew appears on the page.
